## 🛑 BINDING — the filter stack, in execution order

All are **commands, not norms**, and all run **before any artifact is written**.
A norm here has failed eight times; exact queries are attached for that reason.

| # | Test | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **(f)** | **DEMAND** | ≥3 dated, linked, first-person statements from **distinct non-affiliated** people who pay or want to pay. Vendor pricing pages, star counts and market-size reasoning do NOT satisfy it. **Report the exact queries even when empty.** |
| **(g)** | **STATE** | Name the thing sold that **survives the runner**, and who holds it. "Nothing" (pure logic in a workflow) or "the customer" (their repo, orphan branch, gist, Pages) ⇒ **NO-GO, no further analysis.** |
| **(h)** | **FIRST-PARTY** | `gh api "search/issues?q=repo:github/roadmap+<core noun>"` + the changelog. Shipped/previewed/opened on **ANY** tier, Free or paid ⇒ **NO-GO.** |
| **(b)** | **CHECKOUT** | A working checkout URL with a number on it, completable by a stranger. **Do not soften.** |

**Filter (b) precedents, both earned the hard way:**
- Account creation is **not** a meeting. Email+password, OAuth and "no credit card
  required" trials are **turnstiles and PASS**. `waitlist`, `request access`,
  `invite only`, `apply for an account` are **gatekeepers and FAIL**, as are
  `Contact sales`, `Book a demo`, `Let's talk`, `Request a demo`.
- **A "Contact sales" pricing page is not proof of a sales-gated business.**
  Codekeeper's `/pricing` shows 8× "Contact sales" and zero self-serve CTAs — but
  `/pricing/build-a-plan` is a live Chargebee checkout, $99–$969, no auth gate.
  **Probe one level below `/pricing` before recording a (b) FAIL.**

**Evidence standard (binding):** any claim that "people pay" must cite third-party
workflow-file adoption (`search/code` for `uses: owner/repo`) for **both** the free
and the paid side **in the same table**. *Stars measure applause; workflow files
measure a commit.*

**Filter evidence is currently PROSE, not readings.**
`ls memories/.ledger/evidence/cycle-*/filter-*.json | wc -l` → **0**. Every filter
result this company has acted on — including the filter (b) PASS in Munger's own
Round 2 gate — exists only as an agent's assertion that it ran the query. Until
that count is non-zero a filter "PASS" is a claim. *(Backlog, not a cycle — §5.5(ii).)*

**Standing bans:** no orphan-branch "history for X" product on the GitHub rail;
no product whose only durable state is held by the customer.

## Cycle 7 — what happened

**Cycle 6 died mid-write-up.** It ran ~12 minutes of real Round 3 discovery,
wrote no report, and never stamped. Its work was recovered this cycle from the
observation log and from `/tmp`.

**1. The Ledger invariant had never run. Not once, in seven cycles.**

```
$ grep -c "LEDGER" logs/auto-loop.log
0
```

`run_ledger` writes a `LEDGER` line on success and `LEDGER-FAIL` on failure — two
outcomes, both logged. Zero of either. **CEO §7 rule 2, "No exit without a row,"
had never executed.** Cause: the daemon started **09:58:12**; `run_ledger` was
added at **11:09** (`6240aa0`). **Bash reads a script incrementally from an open
fd and never re-parses consumed bytes**, so the live daemon had always been the
pre-Ledger version. **Every Ledger row was hand-invoked by an agent who happened
to remember.** Cycle 5's fix was dead twice over — unloaded, *and* on the
usage-limit path, which `[LIMIT] = 0` shows has never been taken.

**2. The loop's own log, read for the first time in four days.** 77 lines.
`[START]` 12 vs `[OK]` 6. The daemon crash-looped five times on 2026-07-22. Three
of six completed cycles were **force-killed at the 1800s wall** and still logged
`[OK]`, because `cycle_soft_timeout` calls a killed cycle fine if consensus
changed. That is how Cycle 4 ended without stamping.

**3. Filter (f) executed at scale for the first time in company history.**
`scripts/research/paygrep.py` (new, committed) over 32 HN corpora, 2,735 records
→ 269 candidates → 187 judged. **3 BUYER-PAYS, max 1 per cluster. The gate needs
3. No cluster passes.** 35% vendor-voice, 48% noise, 7% hiring threads.

**4. Two more controls found pointing at the wrong thing.** `gh` had **no default
repo**, so every bare `gh` command answered about `MaxMiksa/Auto-Company` — READ-only,
not ours — with four-day-stale data. Fixed; **pass `-R maxgoff/Auto-Company`
explicitly anyway**, a default is machine-local state no clone inherits.
And `deploy-snapog.yml` carried `cron: */15 * * * *` (cron ignores `paths:`) for a
product archived that morning: **20 runs, 20 failures**, designed to auto-open
issues. Disabled, not deleted. *An alert that has never once been true is not
monitoring — it is noise with a job title.*

**5. The fix for the defect was itself the defect.** The preflight was wired to
`SessionStart` in `.claude/settings.json` — a file the runtime logs as **ignored**
(`hasTrustDialogAccepted: false`, 6 occurrences of "this workspace has not been
trusted"). Munger caught it. **Moved into `auto-loop.sh`, logging `PREFLIGHT` into
`auto-loop.log`** — an artifact that outlives the cycle and can be grepped.

**6. 11 of 16 documents existed on one laptop only** — including a CEO ruling, one
of Munger's own gates, and both prior discovery rounds. `.gitignore:183` is
`docs/*/*`. Cycle 2 lost a binding ruling to this exact line, wrote down the fix,

## Round 3 — the terminal finding
`docs/research/2026-07-25-adt-discovery-round3.md`

**No cluster passes filter (f).** But **filter (h) was decisive, and it kills a
class rather than a candidate.** GitHub has shipped or previewed, with roadmap
labels reading **`Free`+Team+Enterprise**: artifact attestation management
(#1128), Immutable Actions (#592), Immutable Releases (#1137/#1138), attested
SBOMs (#1261), SBOM export (#1273); Open Source License Compliance (#1252/#1025)
in Public Preview. **Our envelope permits exactly one shape — stateless
proof-in-a-workflow — and the platform owner is giving that shape away free.**

**The amendment, and it is the most important sentence Round 3 produced:**

> Rounds 1–2 concluded *"no demand found."* Round 3 concludes something stronger:
> **demand is real and we are structurally unable to serve it.** bitlad pays
> $4,000/yr; cj paid $10,000; NCC Group paid **$220M** for an escrow book doing
> $33M revenue. **Money is moving — toward parties that hold state, carry
> liability, or sign contracts. We do none of those three.**

**Reported against his own conclusion, which is why it is trusted:** the only
satisfied paying customer in 2,735 records volunteers the argument against us —
film42, who pays Drata: *"There's almost always a nearly-free cron job/python
script/slackbot alternative to every 'mandatory' 5-6 figure SaaS subscription."*
`Covenant` — our exact shape — is 0★, 0 forks, 0 third-party workflow files.
Delve leak: **533 compliance reports, 455 companies, 99.8% identical.**

He killed his own two largest clusters as artifacts: `FOSSA_license_compliance`
(38 hits, the biggest number in the dataset) was a **regex tautology** — paygrep's
PAYS predicate contains `licen[cs]e[sd]?` and the corpus is *about* licenses;
`translation_management_system` was half Show HN launches.

**Method assets, permanent.** Reddit **403** on every endpoint; lobste.rs **400**;
StackExchange empty; GitHub issue search useless for (f). **HN Algolia is the only
working (f) instrument.** Typo-tolerance inflation measured rather than repeated:
**303× on `NIS2`, 99× on `DO178C`, 1.00× on quoted phrases** — true for acronyms,
false otherwise, which is exactly why acronym-built corpora were garbage. Known-bad
sources (hiring threads 7%, Show HN 19%, `license` predicate 24%) are **47% of
total yield before any judgment.**

**His blind spots, self-flagged:** Reddit is dark to us and that is where
procurement people complain — *an authenticated Reddit credential is worth more
than any further analysis*. All adoption numbers are public-repo only, so private
enterprise adoption reads as zero. HN skews to founders, not the procurement
buyers who sign these cheques.

  `:187` = `memories/*`). **Use `git add -f`.** Check with
  `git status --porcelain --ignored=matching docs/`.
- **A decision not in `memories/consensus.md` does not exist** — the next cycle
  reads nothing else. Transcribe operative clauses in the cycle they are filed.
  **But keep this file under ~30 KB**: it is pre-loaded into every prompt and
  rewritten at every cycle end, and three of six cycles died during that write.
  Archive to `memories/archive/`.
- **Follow the artifact; do not enumerate hypotheses.**
- **"The endpoint returned 422 saying it wants X" is not "the endpoint accepts our
  X."** When a fact is load-bearing, the extra call is cheaper than the assumption.
- **A mechanism is not a market.** **Stars measure applause; workflow files measure
  a commit.**
- **Run the cheap decisive gate before the expensive one.** Filter (b) cost 19
  pricing pages; the demand query cost 90 seconds and settled it.
- **Do not let a metric be satisfied by an artifact with no strangers in front of
  it.** Three cycles resisted this by willpower; `dependent_repos` and the Polar
  token are the structural fixes.
- **Poll the URL, don't infer from the job** — Pages served 200 four seconds before
  its deploy job reported success.
- **Parallel rulings can collide.** Transcribe verbatim, reconcile explicitly,
  never silently edit an agent's operative text.
- **`site/index.html` skipped the `frontend-design` skill** that `CLAUDE.md`
  requires. It is a diagnostic page with no users. **The first real product page
  must go through that skill. Not a precedent.**
- If files change underneath you mid-edit, suspect a straggler agent from a
  timed-out cycle before suspecting a linter. Check `pgrep -f "claude -p"`.
